claim: GFAP-cre;Pik3caH1047R mutant mice exhibit gyrification of the hippocampus and neocortex when induced embryonically.
source: We identified striking gyrification of the hippocampus and neocortex in the embryonically induced GFAP-cre;Pik3caH1047R mutant mice (Figure 1a–l; Roy et al., 2015)
evidence: Supported by histological images in Figure 1 showing cortical folding patterns and by reference to previous work (Roy et al., 2015)

claim: GFAP-cre;Pik3caH1047R mutant mice recapitulate human PI3K-related developmental hydrocephalus without stenosis.
source: This mutant also recapitulates human PI3K-related developmental hydrocephalus, without any evidence of stenosis along the antero-posterior extent of the brain.
evidence: Stated as an observation from the mutant model, supported by morphological analysis

claim: The GFAP-cre driver is activated in neural progenitors at around embryonic day 13.
source: The GFAP-cre driver used in this study gets activated in neural progenitors at around embryonic day (E)13 (Zhuo et al., 2001; Roy et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies (Zhuo et al., 2001; Roy et al., 2015)

claim: The GFAP-cre line demonstrates a strong high-medial-low-lateral expression gradient in the forebrain at E14.5.
source: Around this early activation time, this cre line demonstrates a strong high-medial-low-lateral expression gradient in the forebrain, as well as an apical-low-basal-high gradient within the lateral neocortex, as seen at E14.5 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Supported by expression pattern data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1c

claim: Embryonically induced postnatal day 3 GFAP-cre;Pik3caH1047R mutants demonstrated highly convoluted medial tissue with indistinct hippocampal morphology.
source: Embryonically induced postnatal (P)3 GFAP-cre;Pik3caH1047R mutants (doxycycline: E0.5>P3) demonstrated highly convoluted medial tissue, with indistinct hippocampal morphology (Figure 1b,d,f) (Roy et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by histological images in Figure 1b,d,f and citation to Roy et al., 2015

claim: The hippocampal folding phenotype was 100% penetrant with stereotypic gyral pattern in all mutants studied.
source: This hippocampal folding phenotype was 100% penetrant with stereotypic gyral pattern in all mutants (n > 50) studied.
evidence: Quantitative observation across more than 50 mutant animals

claim: Ventriculomegaly was evident in all mutant brains from as early as E14.5.
source: Ventriculomegaly, indicating developing hydrocephalus, was also clearly evident in all of the mutant brains, seen from as early as E14.5 (Figure 1b,d; Figure 1—figure supplement 2f,p–s; Figure 1—figure supplement 3a,c,e).
evidence: Supported by morphological data shown in multiple figures

claim: Lateral neocortical folding was evident with 100% penetrance but variable in position.
source: Less pronounced lateral neocortical folding was also evident with 100% penetrance, although variable in position (Figure 1b,d; Figure 1—figure supplement 2f–i).
evidence: Observation across all mutants with supporting images

claim: Neocortical and hippocampal folds in Pik3caH1047R mutant mice followed the criteria of bona fide cortical gyrification.
source: Both neocortical and hippocampal folds in the Pik3caH1047R mutant mice followed the criteria of bona fide cortical gyrification (Borrell, 2018): a) folded pial surface and underlying layers, b) predominantly smooth apical surfaces adjacent to the lateral ventricle, c) differential thickness between gyri and sulci (Figure 1—figure supplement 2f–i,p–s).
evidence: Comparison to established criteria from Borrell, 2018 with supporting histological data

claim: Similar lateral and medial cortical gyrification was documented in mice with Pik3caH1047R mutation activated by Emx1-cre.
source: Notably, similar lateral and medial cortical gyrification was also documented in mice with Pik3caH1047R mutation activated by Emx1-cre (D'Gama et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citation to D'Gama et al., 2017

claim: Pik3ca activation is sufficient to cause cortical gyrification across the entire mouse dorsal telencephalon.
source: Together, these data demonstrate that Pik3ca activation is sufficient to cause cortical gyrification across the entire mouse dorsal telencephalon with the phenotype likely dependent on the time and regional gradients of cre activity, and regional differences in neurogenic periods.
evidence: Inference drawn from the collective data presented

claim: P3 Pik3caH1047R mutants showed normally patterned subdivisions of hippocampus proper and dentate gyrus.
source: P3 Pik3caH1047R mutants showed normally patterned subdivisions of hippocampus proper (CA1-4) and dentate gyrus (DG; Figure 1g–l).
evidence: Supported by immunohistochemical data in Figure 1g-l

claim: Gyrification in mutants was primarily restricted to the CA1 region.
source: Ctip2 expression also revealed that the gyrification in mutants was primarily restricted to CA1, with possibly secondary folding evident in the DG.
evidence: Based on Ctip2 expression pattern analysis

claim: The Pik3ca activating mutation resulted in a significant increase in the lengths of P3 CA field and dentate gyrus compared to controls.
source: The Pik3ca activating mutation resulted in a significant increase in the lengths of P3 CA field (p<0.0001) and dentate gyrus (p=0.03), compared to the respective controls (Figure 1—figure supplement 3a,b).
evidence: Quantitative measurement data with statistical significance shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3a,b

claim: The first visual sign of reproducible cortical folding was observed at E16.5 in the Pik3caH1047R mutant dorso-lateral neocortex.
source: The first visual sign of reproducible cortical folding was observed at E16.5 in the Pik3caH1047R mutant dorso-lateral neocortex (Figure 1—figure supplement 3e).
evidence: Temporal observation supported by histological image

claim: E14.5 and E16.5 mutants had significantly longer medial ventricular linings compared to controls.
source: Compared with control, both E14.5 and E16.5 mutants had significantly longer medial ventricular linings (p=0.0028 and p<0.0001 respectively; Figure 1—figure supplement 3c–f), suggesting early expansion of apical progenitors.
evidence: Quantitative measurement with statistical analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 3c-f

claim: E14.5 mutants showed significantly higher proliferation compared to controls, but E16.5 mutants did not.
source: Short BrdU pulse confirmed significantly higher proliferation (p<0.05) in mutants at E14,5, but not at E16.5, compared to respective controls (Figure 2b–e).
evidence: BrdU labeling data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 2b-e

claim: Sox2+ primary progenitors in the mutant CA1 ventricular-subventricular zone were significantly increased at E14.5 and decreased at E16.5.
source: Sox2+ primary progenitors in the mutant CA1 ventricular-subventricular zone were significantly increased at E14.5 (p<0.05) and decreased at E16.5 (p<0.01).
evidence: Quantitative immunohistochemical analysis with statistical significance

claim: Tbr2+ intermediate progenitors were unchanged at E14.5 but significantly increased at E16.5.
source: Tbr2+ IPs) were unchanged at E14.5; but significantly increased at E16.5 (p<0.05), demonstrating a gradual increase in secondary progenitor pool in lieu of the primary progenitors (Figure 2f–i).
evidence: Quantitative immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 2f-i

claim: The number of Sox2+Tbr2- basal radial glia in outer subventricular zone was not significantly different between control and mutant at E16.5.
source: The number of Sox2+Tbr2- bRGs in outer subventricular zone was not significantly different between control and mutant at E16.5 (Figure 2i).
evidence: Quantitative cell counting data shown in Figure 2i

claim: The mutant CA1 demonstrated significantly higher neuronal differentiation at E16.5.
source: The mutant CA1 further demonstrated significantly higher neuronal differentiation at E16.5 (Figure 2j,k).
evidence: Cell cycle exit assay data shown in Figure 2j,k

claim: Birth-dating analysis showed normal neuronal fate specification in P0 mutant CA1.
source: Birth-dating analysis showed normal neuronal fate specification in P0 mutant CA1 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1a–c).
evidence: BrdU birth-dating experiment data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1a-c

claim: A disrupted Nestin+/GFAP+ radial glial scaffold was observed throughout mouse embryogenesis, starting as early as E14.5.
source: Similar to our report of the neocortical phenotype (Roy et al., 2015), we observed a disrupted Nestin+/GFAP+ radial glial scaffold throughout mouse embryogenesis, starting as early as E14.5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d–i).
evidence: Immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d-i and citation to Roy et al., 2015

claim: Postnatal induction of Pik3caH1047R allele failed to cause overtly abnormal brain morphology.
source: Consistent with our previous study (Roy et al., 2015), postnatal induction of Pik3caH1047R allele failed to cause overtly abnormal brain morphology (Figure 3i).
evidence: Morphological observation shown in Figure 3i and citation to Roy et al., 2015

claim: Doxycycline induction from either E0.5 or E13.5 generated the most severely gyrified CA1 with identical stereotypic pattern.
source: By contrast, doxycycline induction from either E0.5 or E13.5 generated the most severely gyrified CA1 with identical stereotypic pattern (Figure 3b–d,k).
evidence: Comparative morphological analysis shown in Figure 3b-d,k

claim: Pik3ca-related ventriculomegaly resulted broadly from mutation induction at any embryonic time point.
source: Pik3ca-related ventriculomegaly resulted broadly from mutation induction at any embryonic time point (Figure 1b,d; Figure 1—figure supplement 2f,p; Figure 1—figure supplement 3a,c,e; Figure 3b–d,f–h; Figure 3—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Morphological observations across multiple time points shown in multiple figures

claim: A short 2 day window of doxycycline administration from E13.5 to E15.5 was sufficient to completely recapitulate the highly stereotypic gyrification pattern.
source: Remarkably, a short 2 day window of doxycycline administration from E13.5 to (>) E15.5 was sufficient to completely recapitulate the highly stereotypic gyrification pattern seen in mutants with constitutive administration of doxycycline throughout development.
evidence: Temporal manipulation experiment demonstrating critical period

claim: Shorter periods of doxycycline treatment within the critical period did not result in gyrification, despite mild cortical dysplasia and ventriculomegaly.
source: Shorter periods of doxycycline treatment (E13.5 > E14.5, E14.5 > E15.5) within this critical period did not result in gyrification, despite mild cortical dysplasia and ventriculomegaly (Figure 3—figure supplement 1b–e).
evidence: Temporal manipulation data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1b-e

claim: Induction beyond E15.5 caused a gradual attenuation of the gyrification phenotype and significantly smaller CA1 pyramidal layer lengths.
source: Induction beyond E15.5 (E15.5 > P3, E15.5 > E17.5, E17.5 > P0) caused a gradual attenuation of the gyrification phenotype and significantly smaller CA1 PL lengths in the respective P3 mutants (Figure 3f–h,k; Figure 3—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Temporal manipulation and quantitative measurement data shown in Figure 3f-h,k and Figure 3—figure supplement 1a

claim: The first obvious morphological sign of CA1 gyrification in minimally induced mutants was a medial 'ripple' at E17.5.
source: The first obvious morphological sign of CA1 gyrification in minimally induced (doxycycline E13.5 > E15.5) mutants was a medial 'ripple' at E17.5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 1f–n).
evidence: Morphological observation shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1f-n

claim: No evidence of ectopic Reelin+ cells was found in either E17.5 or P2 mutant CA1 regions.
source: However, we found no evidence of ectopic Reelin+ cells in either E17.5 or P2 mutant CA1 regions (Figure 2—figure supplement 1m,n; Figure 3—figure supplement 1r,v).
evidence: Immunohistochemical analysis shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1m,n and Figure 3—figure supplement 1r,v

claim: The normal juxtaposition of apical membranes was disrupted in E16.5 mutants, leading to the formation of loose gaps/bubbles along the edge.
source: The normal juxtaposition of apical membranes was disrupted in E16.5 mutants, leading to the formation of loose gaps/bubbles along the edge (Figure 4f–i), which eventually resulted in completely unzippered ventricular linings postnatally (Figure 4—figure supplement 1e–j).
evidence: Immunohistochemical data showing cell adhesion disruption in Figure 4f-i and Figure 4—figure supplement 1e-j

claim: Junctional proteins including β-Catenin, N-Cadherin, and ZO-1 were focally discontinuous and often ectopic in P3 mutants.
source: Junctional proteins delineating the ventricular surface, including β−Catenin, N-Cadherin, ZO-1 (Kadowaki et al., 2007), were focally discontinuous and often ectopic in P3 mutants, compared to their littermate controls.
evidence: Immunohistochemical observation with citation to Kadowaki et al., 2007

claim: Milder disruptions of cell polarity were observed at E16.5 and E14.5 along the mutant medial apical membrane.
source: Milder, yet clear disruptions of cell polarity were observed at E16.5 and E14.5 along the mutant medial apical membrane (Figure 4f–i,o–r).
evidence: Immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 4f-i,o-r

claim: Numerous ectopic Yap+ cells were distributed distal to the mutant CA1 ventricular edge at P3, particularly predominant in the developing gyri.
source: At P3, numerous ectopic Yap+ cells were distributed distal to the mutant CA1 ventricular edge, particularly predominant in the developing gyri (Figure 5e,i,m).
evidence: Immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5e,i,m

claim: Focal concentrations of Yap+ cells were observed in the unzippered areas of the mutant ventricular lining at E16.5, with subtle focal disruption evident as early as E14.5.
source: At E16.5, we observed focal concentrations of Yap+ cells in the unzippered areas of the mutant ventricular lining; subtle focal disruption was evident as early as E14.5 (Figure 5q,t).
evidence: Immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 5q,t

claim: Yap localization was predominantly cytoplasmic and apical at all stages in control mice.
source: Notably, Yap localization was predominantly cytoplasmic (cYap) and apical at all stages in control mice.
evidence: Immunohistochemical observation of Yap subcellular localization

claim: Aberrant nuclear localization of Yap was observed at all stages in mutants, especially evident at P3.
source: In mutants however, we observed aberrant nuclear localization of Yap at all stages, especially evident at P3.
evidence: Immunohistochemical observation of Yap subcellular localization

claim: The total number of nYap+ cells is significantly higher in P3 mutant sulcus and gyrus compared with controls.
source: The total number of nYap+ cells is significantly higher in P3 mutant sulcus and gyrus, compared with the controls (p<0.0001, Figure 5l).
evidence: Quantitative cell counting data with statistical analysis shown in Figure 5l

claim: Verteporfin treatment attenuated the Pik3ca-related gyrification severity and completely rescued ventriculomegaly in 100% of the mutant brains.
source: Morphological analysis at P0 confirmed that verteporfin treatment indeed attenuated the Pik3ca-related gyrification severity and completely rescued ventriculomegaly in 100% of the mutant brains, with little effect on control CA1 ventricular-subventricular zone morphology (Figure 6b–g, Figure 6—figure supplement 1a–h,j).
evidence: Morphological analysis after drug treatment shown in Figure 6b-g and Figure 6—figure supplement 1a-h,j

claim: Principal component analysis revealed that verteporfin administration drives ventricular Pik3ca mutant gene expression towards that of control tissue.
source: Principal component analysis of the global transcriptional profiles of laser micro-dissected P0 CA1 ventricular-subventricular zone tissue (Figure 6e–i) confirmed that the untreated Pik3ca mutant samples (both gyrus and sulcus) were clearly distinct from the control samples. Verteporfin treatment had minimal effect on gene expression of control tissue but shifted the mutant gene expression profiles towards controls.
evidence: RNA sequencing and principal component analysis shown in Figure 6e-i

claim: PI3K and Hippo-Yap signaling pathways were significantly differentially regulated in untreated mutants compared to controls.
source: Gene set enrichment analysis confirmed that PI3K and Hippo-Yap signaling pathways were significantly differentially regulated in untreated mutants compared to controls, as expected (Figure 6—figure supplement 2a–d, Figure 6—source datas 1 and 2).
evidence: Gene set enrichment analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 2a-d

claim: Verteporfin treatment brought both PI3K and Hippo-Yap gene expression in mutants close to control levels, especially at the sulci.
source: Verteporfin treatment brought both PI3K and Hippo-Yap gene expression in mutants close to control levels, especially at the sulci.
evidence: Gene expression analysis from RNA sequencing data

claim: There was considerable overlap in the gyral and sulcal gene expression profiles of Pik3caH1047R mutant mice and those mapped from ferret.
source: Notably, there was a considerable overlap in the gyral and sulcal gene expression profiles of our Pik3caH1047R mutant mice and those mapped from ferret (de Juan Romero et al., 2015) – a naturally gyrencephalic mammal (Figure 6—figure supplement 3a,b).
evidence: Comparative gene expression analysis shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 3a,b with citation to de Juan Romero et al., 2015

claim: Verteporfin normalized apical cell polarity in both the regions of attenuated sulci and gyri in P0 mutants.
source: Immunohistochemical analyses of P0 verteporfin-treated mutants revealed normalized apical cell polarity in both the regions of attenuated sulci and gyri, with elimination of ectopic nYap+ cells and rescue of contiguous apical ZO1 and cYap localization (Figure 7b,c,h–i',n–o').
evidence: Immunohistochemical data after drug treatment shown in Figure 7b,c,h-i',n-o'

claim: Verteporfin normalized both nYap+ and Six3+ cell number and distribution in P0 mutant gyri and sulci.
source: Verteporfin normalized both nYap+ and Six3+ cell number and distribution in P0 mutant gyri and sulci (Figure 6—figure supplement 1k,l; Figure 7h',n',t,u).
evidence: Quantitative immunohistochemical data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1k,l and Figure 7h',n',t,u

claim: The 5 day acute verteporfin treatment of mutant mice resulted in streamlined Vimentin+/Nestin+ radial glia, denser CA1 pyramidal layer cell packing and reduction in the Tbr2+ basal progenitor pool to almost control levels.
source: The 5 day acute verteporfin treatment of mutant mice resulted in streamlined Vimentin+/Nestin+ radial glia, denser CA1 PL cell packing and reduction in the Tbr2+ basal progenitor pool to almost control levels (Figure 7d–g,j–m',p–s',v).
evidence: Immunohistochemical data after drug treatment shown in Figure 7d-g,j-m',p-s',v

claim: TUNEL assay showed no significant difference in apoptotic cell number between E16.5 control and mutant CA1, both in untreated and in verteporfin-treated conditions.
source: TUNEL assay showed no significant difference in apoptotic cell number between E16.5 control and mutant CA1, both in untreated and in verteporfin-treated conditions, indicating that cell death is not an important factor influencing the mutant phenotypes (Figure 7—figure supplement 2h).
evidence: TUNEL assay data shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 2h

claim: A brief embryonic Pik3ca activation was sufficient to drive subtle changes in apical cell adhesion and subcellular Yap translocation.
source: We demonstrate that a brief embryonic Pik3ca activation was sufficient to drive subtle changes in apical cell adhesion and subcellular Yap translocation, causing focal proliferation and subsequent initiation of the stereotypic 'gyrification sequence', seen in naturally gyrencephalic mammals.
evidence: Summary of experimental findings from temporal manipulation and cellular analyses

claim: Treatment with verteporfin restored apical surface integrity, normalized proliferation, attenuated gyrification and rescued the associated hydrocephalus.
source: Treatment with verteporfin, a nuclear Yap inhibitor, restored apical surface integrity, normalized proliferation, attenuated gyrification and rescued the associated hydrocephalus, highlighting the interrelated role of regulated PI3K-Yap signaling in normal neural-ependymal development.
evidence: Summary of verteporfin treatment effects across multiple phenotypes

claim: Apical cell-adhesion is the earliest known substrate for cortical gyrification.
source: Our data defines apical cell-adhesion as the earliest known substrate for cortical gyrification.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from temporal and cellular analyses

claim: Cortical expansion and gyrification have been implicated in the evolution of human cognition.
source: Cortical expansion and gyrification have been implicated in the evolution of human cognition; and dysplastic gyrification is associated with numerous neurodevelopmental disorders including hydrocephalus (Jiménez et al., 2014; Guerra et al., 2015; Gregory et al., 2016; Parrini et al., 2016; Borrell, 2018).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to previous literature

claim: Dysplastic gyrification is associated with numerous neurodevelopmental disorders including hydrocephalus.
source: Cortical expansion and gyrification have been implicated in the evolution of human cognition; and dysplastic gyrification is associated with numerous neurodevelopmental disorders including hydrocephalus (Jiménez et al., 2014; Guerra et al., 2015; Gregory et al., 2016; Parrini et al., 2016; Borrell, 2018).
evidence: Supported by multiple citations to previous literature

claim: Stereotypic, bona fide cortical folding includes formation of gyri and sulci of differential thickness with gyri thicker than the sulci.
source: Stereotypic, bona fide cortical folding includes formation of gyri (away from ventricle) and sulci (proximal to ventricle) of differential thickness (gyri thicker than the sulci), adjacent to a predominantly unfolded apical ventricular lining (Borrell, 2018).
evidence: Definition from Borrell, 2018

claim: Naturally gyrencephalic species undergo a sequence of developmental events referred to as the 'gyrification sequence'.
source: Naturally gyrencephalic species undergo a sequence of developmental events referred to here as the 'gyrification sequence'. It begins with apical progenitor proliferation followed by differential expansion of secondary progenitors, comprising of intermediate precursors (IPs) and basal radial glia cells (bRGs).
evidence: Description of established developmental sequence in gyrencephalic species

claim: Hydrocephalus affects approximately 1 in 1000 births and is among the most common neurodevelopmental disorders.
source: Hydrocephalus, affecting approximately 1 in 1000 births, is among the most common neurodevelopmental disorders with often devastating outcome (Guerra et al., 2015; Tully et al., 2016).
evidence: Epidemiological information supported by citations

claim: Hydrocephalus is characterized by abnormal expansion of brain ventricles and progressive accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid.
source: It is characterized by abnormal expansion of brain ventricles (ventriculomegaly) and progressive accumulation of cerebrospinal fluid (Jiménez et al., 2014; Guerra et al., 2015).
evidence: Clinical definition supported by citations

claim: Current treatment for hydrocephalus requires invasive surgeries with associated significant complications.
source: New therapeutic approaches are urgently needed since current treatment requires invasive surgeries with associated significant complications (Khan et al., 2015).
evidence: Clinical information supported by citation to Khan et al., 2015

claim: PIK3CA-related hydrocephalus is a subtype of developmental hydrocephalus caused by disrupted brain development associated with genetic abnormalities.
source: PIK3CA-related hydrocephalus is a subtype of developmental hydrocephalus, caused by disrupted brain development associated with genetic abnormalities (Tully and Dobyns, 2014; Tully et al., 2016).
evidence: Clinical classification supported by citations

claim: Infantile hydrocephalus can result from environmental insult, including intra-ventricular hemorrhage associated with prematurity.
source: Infantile hydrocephalus can also result from environmental insult, including intra-ventricular hemorrhage associated with prematurity (Adamsbaum et al., 1998; Jiménez et al., 2009).
evidence: Clinical information supported by citations

claim: PI3K activation disrupted apical junctions and caused ectopic subcellular translocation of Yap leading to neural proliferation and gyrification.
source: Here we report that Pik3ca activation in embryonic cortical progenitors during a critical two-day period was sufficient to drive cortical gyrification in mice. PI3K activation disrupted apical junctions and caused ectopic subcellular translocation of Yap leading to neural proliferation and gyrification, as well as abnormal ependymal development and hydrocephalus.
evidence: Summary of main experimental findings

claim: Both the gyrification and hydrocephalus phenotypes were attenuated in the mutant mice by treatment with verteporfin.
source: Both the gyrification and hydrocephalus phenotypes were attenuated in the mutant mice by treatment with verteporfin (US Food and Drug Administration, 2000; Schmidt-Erfurth and Hasan, 2000; Liu-Chittenden et al., 2012), a nuclear Yap inhibitor.
evidence: Summary of drug treatment effects with citations about verteporfin

claim: The PI3K/Hippo-Yap pathway is finely tuned to regulate cell adhesion and proliferation along the apical lining of the forebrain to maintain the lissencephalic mouse brain.
source: These results demonstrate that the PI3K/Hippo-Yap pathway is finely tuned to regulate cell adhesion and proliferation along the apical lining of the forebrain to maintain the lissencephalic mouse brain.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental results

claim: Subtle alterations in the PI3K/Hippo-Yap pathway during the mid-neurogenic phase have dramatic consequences for the cytoarchitecture of forebrain ventricular linings.
source: Subtle alterations in this pathway during the mid-neurogenic phase have dramatic consequences for the cytoarchitecture of forebrain ventricular linings and the interrelated processes of neurogenesis, gyrification and ependymal development.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental results

claim: The activating Pik3caH1047R mutation remains tightly dependent on p85 regulation.
source: Previous studies have demonstrated that Pik3caH1047R allele remains tightly dependent on p85 regulation (Geering et al., 2007; Zhao and Vogt, 2008; Roy et al., 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous studies

claim: The Pik3caH1047R allele is a strongly activating mutation with higher kinase activity but is functionally not an overexpression allele.
source: Hence, although the Pik3caH1047R allele is a strongly activating mutation with higher kinase activity (Gymnopoulos et al., 2007), it is functionally not an overexpression allele to cause massive pathway induction.
evidence: Interpretation of mutation properties with citation to Gymnopoulos et al., 2007

claim: Exquisite PI3K-dependent regulation of apical cell adhesion is essential for normal mouse brain development.
source: Taken together, our data indicate that exquisite PI3K-dependent regulation of apical cell adhesion is essential for normal mouse brain development and suggests that subtle regional changes in other mammals may initiate natural gyrification.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data with speculation about natural gyrification

claim: Focal loss of apical integrity and over-proliferation of neural progenitors in the Pik3ca model highly correlated with focal areas of translocation of Yap protein from the apical cytoplasmic edge to nuclei at the ventricular lining.
source: Focal loss of apical integrity and over-proliferation of neural progenitors in our Pik3ca model highly correlated with focal areas of translocation of Yap protein from the apical cytoplasmic edge to nuclei at the ventricular lining.
evidence: Correlation observed from immunohistochemical and proliferation data

claim: Yap is a central regulator of the Hippo pathway with both nuclear and cytoplasmic functions.
source: Yap is a central regulator of the Hippo pathway, with both nuclear and cytoplasmic functions (Gumbiner and Kim, 2014; Park et al., 2016; Park et al., 2018).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by citations

claim: The Hippo-Yap pathway mediates mechanical signals, cellular stress, polarity and adhesion cues that are integrated through multiple upstream regulators.
source: The Hippo-Yap pathway is known to mediate mechanical signals, cellular stress, polarity and adhesion cues that are integrated through multiple upstream regulators (Hansen et al., 2015).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by citation to Hansen et al., 2015

claim: Phosphorylated Yap is sequestered in the cytoplasm by adherens junction proteins.
source: Phosphorylated Yap is sequestered in the cytoplasm by adherens junction proteins.
evidence: Established molecular mechanism

claim: Cytoplasmic Yap expressed in the early developing ependyma critically maintains cell-cell adhesion at the ventricular edge of ventral aqueduct.
source: In turn, cYap, expressed in the early developing ependyma, has been shown to critically maintain cell-cell adhesion at the ventricular edge of ventral aqueduct (Park et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to Park et al., 2016

claim: When dephosphorylated, Yap translocates to the nucleus where it binds to TEAD transcriptional co-regulators to modulate gene expression.
source: When dephosphorylated, Yap translocates to the nucleus, where it binds to TEAD transcriptional co-regulators to modulate gene expression (Hansen et al., 2015; Park et al., 2018).
evidence: Established molecular mechanism supported by citations

claim: Nuclear Yap was recently shown to be sufficient to drive cortical progenitor proliferation.
source: In this context, nYap was recently shown to be sufficient to drive cortical progenitor proliferation (Lavado et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to Lavado et al., 2018

claim: In vitro, PI3K-PDK1 pathway activation promotes nuclear translocation of Yap, thus disrupting contact inhibition.
source: In vitro, PI3K-PDK1 pathway activation promotes nuclear translocation of Yap, thus disrupting contact inhibition (Fan et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to Fan et al., 2013

claim: Verteporfin disintegrates the Yap-TEAD nuclear complex, facilitating sequestration of Yap to the cytoplasm.
source: Verteporfin, a nYap antagonist, disintegrates the Yap-TEAD nuclear complex, facilitating sequestration of Yap to the cytoplasm (US Food and Drug Administration, 2000; Schmidt-Erfurth and Hasan, 2000; Liu-Chittenden et al., 2012; Fan et al., 2013; Brodowska et al., 2014; Gumbiner and Kim, 2014).
evidence: Mechanism of drug action supported by multiple citations

claim: This is the first study where verteporfin was introduced intraperitoneally into pregnant mice to successfully suppress nYap function in embryos across the placental barrier.
source: To our knowledge, this is the first study where verteporfin was introduced intraperitoneally into the pregnant mice to successfully suppress nYap function in embryos across the placental barrier.
evidence: Novel methodological approach claimed by authors

claim: The gyrification phenotype was not fully rescued, likely because PI3K signaling has a multitude of downstream outputs in addition to Yap regulation.
source: We did not fully rescue the gyrification phenotype, likely because PI3K signaling has a multitude of downstream outputs in addition to Yap regulation.
evidence: Interpretation of incomplete rescue with speculation about mechanism

claim: PI3K pathway modulation of the cytoplasmic Yap pool during the brief embryonic critical period is essential to maintain the lissencephalic mouse brain.
source: Although we cannot rule out potential off-target effects of verteporfin, our data provide strong evidence that PI3K pathway modulation of the cYap pool during the brief embryonic critical period is essential to maintain the lissencephalic mouse brain.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data with acknowledgment of limitations

claim: Subtle changes in local apical adhesion properties of early progenitors, associated with focal changes in Yap subcellular distribution and subsequently in the basal progenitor population, is one of the initiating mechanisms of gyrification in higher mammals.
source: We speculate that subtle changes in local apical adhesion properties of early progenitors, associated with focal changes in Yap subcellular distribution and subsequently in the basal progenitor population, is one of the initiating mechanisms of gyrification in higher mammals.
evidence: Speculation based on experimental findings

claim: YAP maintains basal progenitor population in the developing ferret and human neocortex.
source: Further, a recent study has demonstrated that YAP maintains basal progenitor population in the developing ferret and human neocortex (Kostic et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kostic et al., 2019

claim: YAP regulation by verteporfin in ex vivo embryonic ferret and fetal human neocortical tissue culture systems leads to reduction in basal progenitor number.
source: Similar to our current findings, this study also showed that YAP regulation by verteporfin in ex vivo embryonic ferret and fetal human neocortical free-floating tissue culture systems leads to reduction in basal progenitor number (Kostic et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citation to Kostic et al., 2019

claim: Cortical folding patterns in naturally gyrencephalic species are highly stereotypic, although there is considerable inter-individual variation.
source: Cortical folding patterns in naturally gyrencephalic species are highly stereotypic, although there is considerable inter-individual variation (Ronan and Fletcher, 2015; Borrell, 2018).
evidence: Established knowledge supported by citations

claim: The gyrification pattern induced in GFAP-cre;Pik3caH1047R mutants was non-random with 100% penetrance and was highly cre-dependent.
source: Importantly, the gyrification pattern induced in GFAP-cre;Pik3caH1047R mutants was non-random, with 100% penetrance, and was highly cre-dependent (Roy et al., 2015; D'Gama et al., 2017).
evidence: Observation from experimental data with citations

claim: Cell-cell adhesion is less constrained in susceptible focal positions compared to adjacent regions during the critical periods of development.
source: We hypothesize that cell-cell adhesion is less constrained in susceptible focal positions compared to adjacent regions during the critical periods of development.
evidence: Hypothesis proposed by authors

claim: The highly regulatable stereotypical and fully penetrant gyrification phenotype of Pik3caH1047R mutant mice provides a new, highly tractable alternative model to unravel the positional constraints giving rise to brain folds.
source: The highly regulatable stereotypical and fully penetrant gyrification phenotype of Pik3caH1047R mutant mice provides a new, highly tractable alternative model to unravel the positional constraints giving rise to brain folds.
evidence: Conclusion about the utility of the model

claim: Embryonic induction of Pik3caH1047R allele in mouse neural progenitors caused ventriculomegaly which progressed postnatally to hydrocephalus.
source: In addition to gyrification, embryonic induction of Pik3caH1047R allele in mouse neural progenitors also caused ventriculomegaly which progressed postnatally to hydrocephalus.
evidence: Observation from experimental data

claim: Hydrocephalus is a common feature of human PI3K-related brain overgrowth syndromes.
source: Hydrocephalus is a common feature of human PI3K-related brain overgrowth syndromes (Mirzaa et al., 2012; Tully and Dobyns, 2014; Guerra et al., 2015; Khan et al., 2015).
evidence: Clinical information supported by multiple citations

claim: PI3K-dependent ventriculomegaly had a long embryonic critical period ending at E17.5, compared to the short gyrification critical period (E13.5-E15.5).
source: We determined that PI3K-dependent ventriculomegaly had long embryonic critical period, ending at E17.5, compared to the short gyrification critical period (E13.5-E15.5).
evidence: Temporal analysis from experimental data

claim: Embryonic verteporfin-dependent nYap inhibition rescued ventriculomegaly with minimal effect on control littermates.
source: Embryonic verteporfin-dependent nYap inhibition also rescued ventriculomegaly, with minimal effect on control littermates.
evidence: Drug treatment experiment results

claim: Disrupted apical cell adhesion and aberrant nYap localization were central to the hydrocephalus phenotype as well as gyrification.
source: We conclude that disrupted apical cell adhesion and aberrant nYap localization were central to this phenotype as well as gyrification.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental results

claim: Hydrocephalus is often associated with a disrupted ependyma, although in many cases it is unclear if this is because of abnormal ependymal development or ependymal damage at a later stage.
source: Hydrocephalus is often associated with a disrupted ependyma, although in many cases it is unclear if this is because of abnormal ependymal development or ependymal damage at a later stage (Jiménez et al., 2014).
evidence: Clinical knowledge with citation to Jiménez et al., 2014

claim: The ependyma is a continuous single layer of neuroepithelial multi-ciliated cells lining the lateral ventricles.
source: The ependyma is a continuous single layer of neuroepithelial multi-ciliated cells lining the lateral ventricles.
evidence: Anatomical definition

claim: Ependymal cells differentiate from apical progenitors and mature during late embryogenesis and early postnatal mouse development.
source: Ependymal cells differentiate from apical progenitors and mature during late embryogenesis and early postnatal mouse development, when most definitive ependymal markers, including FoxJ1 and other markers of multi-ciliated cells, are expressed (Schmidt-Erfurth and Hasan, 2000; Lavado and Oliver, 2011).
evidence: Developmental biology knowledge supported by citations

claim: The normally uniform layer of Vimentin+/Yap+ developing ependymal cells was disrupted at mid-embryonic stages in the mutant mouse model.
source: In our mutant mouse model, the normally uniform layer of Vimentin+/Yap+ developing ependymal cells was disrupted at mid-embryonic stages.
evidence: Immunohistochemical observation

claim: Cells with ependymal fate (Yap+) were intermingled with Tbr2+ progenitors and young Ctip2+ neurons at the mutant gyral edge, indicating abnormal neural-to-ependymal transition.
source: Further, cells with ependymal fate (Yap+) were intermingled with Tbr2+ progenitors and young Ctip2+ neurons at the mutant gyral edge, indicating abnormal neural-to-ependymal transition.
evidence: Immunohistochemical observation with interpretation

claim: The hydrocephalus phenotype was reversed with verteporfin treatment, although the drug-treated ependyma was not entirely normal.
source: This phenotype and the subsequent hydrocephalus were reversed with verteporfin treatment, although the drug-treated ependyma was not entirely normal.
evidence: Drug treatment experiment results

claim: Early Yap-dependent apical adhesion is required for normal ependymal development in forebrain during embryonic pre-ciliogenesis stages.
source: These data clearly demonstrate that early Yap-dependent apical adhesion is required for normal ependymal development in forebrain during embryonic pre-ciliogenesis stages – a developmental time much earlier than previously established.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from experimental data

claim: Human post-mortem studies and in vitro model studies have shown disruption of cell adhesion and apical junctions in post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus.
source: Interestingly, human post-mortem studies and in vitro model studies have shown disruption of cell adhesion and apical junctions in post-hemorrhagic hydrocephalus, a common form of hydrocephalus in premature infants, currently with few treatment options (Morales et al., 2012; Jiménez et al., 2014; Guerra et al., 2015).
evidence: Clinical and experimental findings supported by citations

claim: In mice, embryonic intraventricular administration of blood-derived lysophosphatidic acid is sufficient to cause disrupted ependymal cell adhesion and neonatal hydrocephalus.
source: In mice, embryonic intraventricular administration of blood-derived lysophosphatidic acid (LPA), is sufficient to cause disrupted ependymal cell adhesion and neonatal hydrocephalus in mice (Yung et al., 2015).
evidence: Experimental finding supported by citation to Yung et al., 2015

claim: Depletion of cytoplasmic YAP by either genetic deletion or LPA treatment resulted in perinatal hydrocephalus due to impaired ependymal development and aqueduct blockage.
source: More recently, Park et al. (2016) showed that depletion of cYAP, by either genetic deletion or LPA treatment, also resulted in perinatal hydrocephalus due to impaired ependymal development and aqueduct blockage (Park et al., 2016).
evidence: Experimental finding supported by citation to Park et al., 2016

claim: Altered periventricular cell adhesion caused by dysregulated Hippo-Yap signaling is a common convergent mechanism for both developmental and post hemorrhagic hydrocephalus.
source: Taken together with our data, we posit that altered periventricular cell adhesion caused by dysregulated Hippo-Yap signaling is a common convergent mechanism for both developmental and post hemorrhagic hydrocephalus.
evidence: Conclusion drawn from integration of current data with previous literature

claim: Fine regulation of the Hippo-Yap pathway may represent a new therapeutic approach for pediatric hydrocephalus patients.
source: Fine regulation of the Hippo-Yap pathway may represent a new therapeutic approach for pediatric hydrocephalus patients, especially since verteporfin effectively crosses the placenta and has minimal effect on normal brain development as demonstrated by our morphological and RNA-seq analyses.
evidence: Therapeutic implication based on experimental findings

claim: Verteporfin effectively crosses the placenta and has minimal effect on normal brain development.
source: Fine regulation of the Hippo-Yap pathway may represent a new therapeutic approach for pediatric hydrocephalus patients, especially since verteporfin effectively crosses the placenta and has minimal effect on normal brain development as demonstrated by our morphological and RNA-seq analyses.
evidence: Observation from drug treatment experiments

claim: Disruption of apical surface integrity in the forebrain via enhanced embryonic PI3K-Yap signaling alters neurogenesis and can initiate bona fide gyrification in mice.
source: In summary, building upon our original study of mouse models of human PIK3CA-related brain malformations (Roy et al., 2015), we demonstrate intimate PI3K-dependent developmental and molecular links between cortical neurogenesis and ependymal development at the apical edge of the embryonic ventricular zone. Disruption of apical surface integrity in the forebrain, via enhanced embryonic PI3K-Yap signaling, alters neurogenesis and can initiate bona fide gyrification in mice.
evidence: Summary conclusion from experimental findings

claim: Abnormal apical PI3K-Yap interaction disrupts ependymal development in forebrain prior to ciliogenesis, leading to hydrocephalus.
source: Concurrently, abnormal apical PI3K-Yap interaction disrupts ependymal development in forebrain, prior to ciliogenesis, leading to hydrocephalus.
evidence: Summary conclusion from experimental findings

claim: The data readily explain the coincidence of impaired neurogenesis, gyrification and hydrocephalus observed often in patients with cortical dysplasia and in the Pik3ca mouse model.
source: Our data readily explain the coincidence of impaired neurogenesis, gyrification and hydrocephalus, observed often in patients with cortical dysplasia and in our Pik3ca mouse model (Keppler-Noreuil et al., 2014; Jansen et al., 2015; Roy et al., 2015; Parrini et al., 2016; Furey et al., 2018).
evidence: Conclusion linking experimental findings to clinical observations with citations

claim: The results provide support for nuclear Yap protein as a potential new therapeutic target for cortical dysplasia disorders.
source: The results also provide support for nuclear Yap protein as a potential new therapeutic target for these clinically important disorders.
evidence: Therapeutic implication based on experimental findings
